episodes.158270: A thunderstorm produced a localized damaging downburst near Petersburg.
episodes.158285: An unseasonably cool and wet pattern persisted across New Mexico at the end of June 2021 and resulted in several inches of rainfall across the southeastern portion of the state. With a large trough across the Rockies and easterly flow across much of New Mexico, moisture continued to stream into the area which allowed for daily rounds of showers and thunderstorms. On June 28, 2021, about 2 to 4 inches of rain fell across southern Chaves County. This amount of rainfall in a short period of time resulted in localized flooding which forced the closure of New Mexico State Road 2 near Lake Arthur.
episodes.158325: Thunderstorms moving across coastal waters produce strong wind gusts.
episodes.158398: Bright sunshine, combined with high humidity and very warm temperatures, led to a moderately to highly unstable atmosphere by the late afternoon of June 28th. In this primed environment, a weak shortwave, traversing the southwest periphery of a strong upper level high situated over the Mid-Atlantic, sparked scattered pulse-type storms through much of the evening. While almost all of the storms developed and dissipated quickly, the strongest and most persistent storm of the day moved from Virginia into Pike County and produced torrential downpours, nearly continuous lightning, and some severe wind damage before dissipating near Pikeville.
episodes.158404: Intense moisture in the atmosphere combined with strong surface outflow boundaries to create a landspout tornado in Hockley County near Opdyke West. This landspout tornado caused no known damage as it remained over an open field.
episodes.158405: A tropical like atmosphere continued to remain over the region on the 28th which was able to produce showers that were efficient rainfall producers. On the morning of the 28th, heavy rain showers repeatedly trained over the eastern half of Garza County causing flash flooding in and around Lake Alan Henry (Garza County). The Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site at Lake Alan Henry measured 5.18 inches of rainfall in a three hour period. The Garza County sheriff's office reported water running over US Highway 84 between Post and Justiceburg. Additionally, some structures became inundated near Lake Alan Henry.
episodes.158452: A broad, moist southwesterly flow from the surface to the mid-levels fueled scattered afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms across much of the region.  A strong storm produced a severe wind gust.
episodes.158461: Early on the 28th, showers and thunderstorms developed in an anomalously moist environment, with precipitable water values reaching up to 2 inches. One large storm developed, producing very heavy rainfall in Scotland and Clark Counties, eventually dying off as it continued to move east. This storm dropped upwards to 3 inches or more, which led to flash flooding in mainly rural area. Roads were washed out with several inches of water, making them impassable.
episodes.158469: Thunderstorms that developed in the late afternoon hours of June 28 produced wind gusts that brought down numerous trees and power lines across parts of East Tennessee.
episodes.158470: A thunderstorm produced wind gusts that brought down trees and power lines across parts of Wise County.
episodes.158805: A plume of deep tropical moisture associated with a mid-level trough advected westward across South Florida from the Bahamas. Weak steering flow allowed for several rounds of storms to move slowly across Miami-Dade, which resulted in flooding from heavy rainfall.
episodes.158807: A plume of deep tropical moisture associated with a mid-level trough advected westward across South Florida from the Bahamas. During peak heating in the afternoon, thunderstorms developed across the Gulf Coast. One of these storms produced a strong wind gust as it moved offshore.
episodes.159126: A slow-moving cold front interacting with a warm and very humid airmass resulted in scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening of June 27th.  One cluster of storms dropped heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches in Mattoon in Coles County, causing localized flash flooding and a few road closures.
episodes.159579: Persistent and heavy rain caused flash flooding in Anderson County during the afternoon of 6/28.
episodes.159588: Isolated thunderstorms produced heavy rain which caused localized flooding.
episodes.159649: A very moist airmass and slow moving storms led to a multi-day heavy rainfall event for much of the area. 6 to 8+ inches fell in a swath from southwest OK northeast along the I-44 corridor. Several storms also produced isolated severe weather with hail and strong winds reported.
episodes.159650: A very moist airmass and slow moving storms led to a multi-day heavy rainfall event for much of the area. 6 to 8+ inches fell in a swath from southwest OK northeast along the I-44 corridor. Several storms also produced isolated severe weather with hail and strong winds reported.
episodes.159693: Tropical Storm Danny initially developed as a tropical depression approximately 110 miles off the Southeast United States coast during the morning of June 28th, 2021, slowly tracking west-northwest across warmer gulf stream waters and eventually reaching tropical storm strength at 305 PM on June 28th, 2021 approximately 40 miles off the South Carolina coast. Danny made landfall at 8:00 PM just north of Hilton Head on Pritchards Island, South Carolina with a minimum central pressure of 1010 MB or 29.82 inches. After landfall, Danny continued moving to the west-northwest, eventually weakening to a tropical depression near the South Carolina/Georgia state line and following a path across central Georgia.  The primary impacts from Danny included gusty winds and heavy rainfall. Across Jasper and Beaufort counties, rainfall total amounts ranged approximately 3.50 to 6.25 inches, causing minor flooding issues across highways. Winds peaked over the Atlantic coastal waters with a 41 knot wind gust measured at Buoy 41029. Otherwise, wind gusts generally ranged between  the 25 to 40 mph across coastal counties of southeast South Carolina, producing isolated/minor wind damage across Charleston County.
episodes.159694: Tropical Storm Danny initially developed as a tropical depression approximately 110 miles off the Southeast United States coast during the late morning of June 28th, 2021, slowly tracking west-northwest across warmer gulf stream waters and eventually reaching tropical storm strength at 305 PM on June 28th, 2021 approximately 70 miles off the Georgia coast. Danny made landfall at 8:00 PM just north of Hilton Head on Pritchards Island, South Carolina with a minimum central pressure of 1010 MB or 29.82 inches. After landfall, Danny continued moving to the west-northwest, eventually weakening to a tropical depression near the South Carolina/Georgia state line and following a path across central Georgia. The primary impacts from Danny included gusty winds and heavy rainfall. Across Chatham and Effingham counties, rainfall total amounts ranged approximately 3.25 to 5.50 inches. Winds peaked over the Atlantic coastal waters with a 41 knot wind gust measured at Buoy 41029. Otherwise, wind gusts generally ranged between 25 to 40 mph across Chatham County, producing isolated/minor wind damage.
episodes.159873: Heavy rainfall affected the same region as rains earlier in the week, leading to additional flooding of some areas.
episodes.159908: Warm, humid conditions and a passing, weak disturbance across Central New York supported some scattered thunderstorms. A couple of which became severe. The majority of the reports came from Oneida County where there were reports of trees, wires, and utility poles down.
episodes.160072: An upper level low pressure system was over the Arizona and New Mexico border. There was a stationary front across the area which provided additional lift over West Texas. Abundant moisture was continuing to move into the region. These conditions resulted in rain and thunderstorms developing and moving over the same areas producing flash flooding across West Texas.
episodes.160073: An upper level low pressure system was over the Arizona and New Mexico border. There was a stationary front across the area which provided additional lift over Southeast New Mexico. Abundant moisture was continuing to move into the region. These conditions resulted in rain and thunderstorms developing and moving over the same areas producing flash flooding across Southeast New Mexico.
episodes.160171: A fairly typical summertime setup was in place with ample moisture available and strong daytime heating. The local morning upper air sounding noted a mid level region of drier air. It's suspected that this mid level drying enhanced down drafts in storms over Lake Pontchartrain and produced gusty winds that exceeded gale force.
episodes.160228: Heavy rain produced some marginal flash flooding in Miami County Kansas and nearby Bates County Missouri.
episodes.160229: Heavy rain produced some marginal flash flooding in Miami County Kansas and nearby Bates County Missouri.
episodes.160275: A thunderstorm produced heavy rain and flash flooding in the Calwood burn area.  Law enforcement reported a 3 to 4 foot surge of debris and water flowing down Geer Canyon. |The debris flow impacted stretches of Geer Canyon Drive and the lower part of Geer Canyon.
episodes.160354: Deep monsoonal moisture moved into the region and combined with an upper level trough to produce training storms across the city of El Paso which resulted in one death.
episodes.160357: A large upper level ridge remained off the east coast of the United States, allowing southerly flow to stream north from the Gulf of Mexico, across the Mississippi Valley, and into the lower Great Lakes region. Temperatures in the Southern Tier were in the mid 80s with dewpoints near 70 degrees.  Shear aloft was minimal, but there was plenty of instability. Overall, convection was expected to be sub-severe and initiating on lake breeze boundaries. This was the case until one cell grew rapidly in the warm and unstable environment over the Southern Tier, necessitating a warning.
episodes.160485: A severe thunderstorm produced hail across portions of Grant County during the mid to late afternoon.
episodes.160512: Thunderstorms developed over the Mogollon Rim and moved southwest across Greenlee and Graham counties.  One storm caused lightning and wind damage in Central.
episodes.160631: Fresh east to southwest winds in combination with enhanced upper divergence from an upper low pressure system in the western Gulf of Mexico resulted in gale-force wind gusts in westward-moving thunderstorms along the Upper and Lower Florida Keys.
episodes.160632: Gale-force wind gusts occurred with thunderstorms occurring along the Lower Florida Keys.  Rich tropical moisture was in place with weakly-cyclonic flow aloft.
episodes.160804: A quasi-stationary front across the region triggered scattered showers and storms. Some of the storms were severe with several reports of damaging winds.
